terms.grammar: genitive of regiō, regiōnis f., with a demonstrative: ējus regiōnis, eārum regiōnum
evidence: Caes. BG 5.20.1: firmissima eārum regiōnum cīvitās
terms.comment: Latin uses the genitive of the noun where English has an adjective: the strongest people of that region. For the region itself, see area.

evidence: Varr. LL 5.77: aquātilium vocābula partim sunt vernācula partim peregrīna (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Home-grown, native, as against foreign (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens gives ferculum vernāculum for a regional dish. Its first sense is of a slave born in the house, verna.
Augustine’s word for a provincial council of the Church, as against a plenary one (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: regio · Lewis & Short: vernaculus · Lewis & Short: regionalis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. local.
Caesar, Gallic War 5.20, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026).
